editions.title: GitHub Actions will happily run YAML your parser rejects
editions.excerpt: GitHub's workflow parser is more forgiving than any YAML tool you have locally, which means broken workflow files can pass every check and still behave strangely.

editions.title: RHEL runners go GA, so your CI can match what you ship
editions.excerpt: GitHub's larger runners now offer generally available RHEL 9 and 10 images, so testing on the OS you deploy to no longer means keeping a self-hosted box alive.

editions.title: Azure DevOps migrations now keep working while you keep working
editions.excerpt: Enterprise Live Migrations to GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency is generally available; first, learn what is actually in the repo you're moving.

editions.title: GitHub's new PR overview stops optional checks from crying wolf
editions.excerpt: The improved Overview page no longer lets failed optional checks masquerade as blockers, which makes it a fine day to find the automation in your repo that stares at pull requests.

editions.title: GitHub CLI can finally wait for a pull request to change
editions.excerpt: gh v2.105.0 adds event streams, so scripts and agents can subscribe to reviews and checks instead of sleeping in a polling loop.

editions.title: Cloudflare opened the hood on its agent browser engine
editions.excerpt: Kitesurf, an experimental browser engine built for AI agents, is now open source. You can read it, run it, or host your own copy on Workers.

editions.title: The harness is not the model.
editions.excerpt: A read-only audit for the layer between your editor and your model provider. Includes a runnable script and a prompt for your coding agent.
